Additionally, historical patterns of violence and external pressures from neighboring countries complicate the situation. Lasting peace in Ethiopia requires a consensus on power-sharing and improved diplomatic relations with its neighbors, addressing both internal divisions and external tensions.

According to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) October 2026 World Economic Outlook, Kenya has surpassed Ethiopia to become East Africa's largest economy in nominal GDP terms, primarily due to currency exchange rate fluctuations rather than faster economic growth. While Ethiopia's real GDP grew by 9.2% in 2025, Kenya's growth was only 4.6%. The depreciation of the Ethiopian birr, following a shift to a market-determined exchange-rate system, significantly reduced the dollar value of its economy. In contrast, Kenya's stronger shilling contributed to a 13.7% increase in its nominal GDP in dollar terms. The IMF projects continued growth for both economies, with Ethiopia expected to maintain higher real GDP growth rates compared to Kenya. The nominal GDP per capita is estimated at $1,130 for Ethiopia and $2,790 for Kenya in 2026.
